entry.title: FC 26 Web app: Are EA Account servers down
entry.summary:
The Web app for FC 26 is available on PC for all, but the servers aren't working as intended for many at the time of writing.
The Web app is many people's first introduction to this year's Ultimate Team. Users can create their starter squads, complete the beginner SBCs, and more for free. All their progress will be carried over when they later resume their journeys in the game.
However, the servers being out of order is creating problems for many.
When did the FC 26 Web App servers go down?
The exact time is hard to pinpoint, but it appears to have happened right after the servers went live at 6 pm BST. This is the typical content time followed by EA Sports for releasing content in Ultimate Team. I did manage to sign in for a brief period and was taken to the screen for selecting the starter league pack.
Unfortunately, my choice couldn't register due to the current situation with the servers. Since then, all my attempts to successfully log onto the app have failed. It appears that I am not the only one, as social media platforms like X have plenty of examples like mine.
Unfortunately, the servers have gone down in the past. This happens mainly because too many players are trying to sign in at the exact moment, overloading the servers. At the time of writing, it's impossible to predict when the servers will be functional again.
Once the servers are restored, you'll be able to log in to your account and start building up your Ultimate Team squad. The best course of action is to wait till the load stabilizes.

Elder Scrolls Online developers ZeniMax Online Studios were among those making cuts - they buried an unannounced project codenamed Blackbird, which was reportedly a nimble MMO shooter of some kind. Unionised staff members have described the reductions as "inhumane", demoralising and counterproductive, with one worker commenting that "a lot of practical knowledge just disappeared overnight".
Now, studio game director Rich Lambert and game director Nick Giacomini have been chatting a little about where ZeniMax Online Studios is going next. entry.title: How to fly in Skate – Take the Plunge guide
entry.summary:
The Take the Plunge goal in Skate can be a bit tricky to complete since one of its tasks requires you to fly through the gaps in a bridge.
While the game has plenty of high-flying moves, they're usually performed with your skateboard. The task at hand, compared to those moves, has to be pulled off without one. Moreover, you'll have to pay attention to your movement in the air to complete the objective successfully.
How do you fly through the bridge supports in Skate?
The task at hand requires you to fly through the bridge supports. The first job is to travel to the top of the house, as marked on the map. Once you reach the location, you can then complete the three tasks (separately). The second of the three tasks is to fly through the bridge supports.
Screenshot by Destructoid
To fly, first start a sprint with the LS key. This will help you gain speed before jumping into the air.
When in the air, press the R1/RB button to start a dive. The dive will allow you to travel over longer distances and help you reach the target location.
Now press R1/RB and the X/A buttons together to perform the Spread Eagle move.
When you land on the spot, you might miss the exact mark. In that case, you will aim to use the ragdoll effects and momentum to carry your body forward slightly. If you fly and land in the correct locations, you'll be taken back to the starting spot.
After flying in Skate, you must hit two locations. If you miss the spot at first, keep trying until you succeed. If you hit the location and the quest doesn't track your progress, try out this fix to solve the problem. Also, ensure that the servers are operational, since that can also prevent you from successfully flying and completing the Take the Plunge goal.

entry.title: How to fix Skate ‘connection lost’ error – Error code 3967269002
entry.summary:
It's been a long time coming, but it appears the wait will be even longer than anticipated.
Skating fans around the world are stoked to be back in the world of Skate for the first time in many years. They are so excited, in fact, that the game is breaking underneath the weight of gamers trying to connect, and it's causing error codes galore.
Here's what we know so far about issues with Skate, including the error code 3967269002.
How to fix Skate error code 3967269002
Screenshot by Destructoid
The Skate error code 3967269002 is happening a lot on the day of the game's free-to-play launch on Sept. 16, 2025. It's most likely due to the game's servers being slammed by players attempting to log in all at once and/or download the game since there was no pre-load.
So far, we've been able to have success in getting into the game by just selecting "OK" and entering a new queue. As the game is being overloaded, players are being placed into a queue, and sometimes those queues are erroring out. Your best bet for now is to try re-queuing and getting into the game.
Odds are, though, that these errors, server issues, and queues will all need to be fixed by EA, and there's not much you can do as a player besides waiting it out. In this always-online world of online gaming, these things tend to happen around big launches or updates, so it comes as no surprise that there are problems with playing the game.
Stay tuned to official EA communications for more info on the status of the game's servers, especially in its first few days and weeks following launch.

entry.title: Troublemaker 2 is an exuberant and janky Indonesian open world game with a touch of Like A Dragon
entry.summary:
I'm not sure the just-released Troublemaker 2: Beyond Dream is one of those "good games" you're all so bloody obsessed with. My working summary, based on 30 minutes with the demo, is that it's an unofficial Like A Dragon/Yakuza game developed with a fraction of the budget, and set in "fictionalised" Indonesia. That's to say, it's an open world comedy beat 'em up with a bunch of other genres haphazardly stirred in.
I compared it to Rockstar's work and Saints Row in this week's Maw, which was Mostly Wrong. This is a predominantly on-foot experience, for one thing, and you can't grievously assault people at random. There are designated gangs of hoodlums you're permitted to punch out, and as far as I can tell, you have to wait for them to Make Trouble first. It seems very polite and passive for a brawler. Also, you get to transform briefly into a dying cow.

entry.title: Announcing support for World Builder-based games
entry.summary: After many years of development, games made with World Builder are ready for testing. The World Builder creation system was released for the original Macintosh and was extremely popular among developers. As such, we're announcing that over 160 games built on the engine are ready for public testing in ScummVM. Notable games made with World Builder include: Ray's Maze. The game follows Frank Farley, a part-time adventurer, who finds himself in a Maze full of dangerous monsters and deadly traps. The objective of the game is to solve puzzles and escape the maze. Radical Castle. You are given the role of a squire, who must bring back the stolen "Oracle" to the King to escape a fatal punishment. Enchanced Scepters. The first game created using World Builder, and one of the few commercial games made with it. The player must find fire, earth, air, and water scepters and bring them back to the castle. Most games made with WAGE are either freeware or shareware, and for your convenience we've collected all titles with these types into one big downloadable archive. So grab it from our game downloads page, get yourself a daily development build, and start your journey. As always, if you happen to have any issues, please submit the bug reports to our issue tracker. Lastly, contact us if you have some other unrecognised games or a new demo. >
